chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Abd al-Samad ibn Bashir, from al-Fadil ibn Sukkarah, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): May I be your ransom! If you see fit to teach me: Did Allah, may His Remembrance be Exalted, know before He created the creation that He was alone? Your followers have differed regarding this. Some of them said: 'The Blessed and Exalted surely knew that He was alone before He created anything from His creation.' And some of them said: 'The meaning of 'He knows' is 'He does'; so He knows today that there is no other before the doing of things.' And they said: 'If we affirm that He has always been Knowing that there is no other, then we have affirmed with Him an 'other' in His eternity.' If you see fit, O my Master, to teach me what is not other than this, so he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'Allah, the Exalted, has always been Knowing, Blessed and Exalted be His Remembrance.'
ai.seo_question: Did Allah know He was One before creating the universe?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this dialogue with Imam al-Jawad (or al-Kazim, depending on the chain's specific attribution in al-Tawhid) to resolve the Mu'tazilite concern that affirming eternal knowledge of a non-existent 'other' implies co-eternity with that other. The Imam’s concise affirmation that 'Allah has always been All-Knowing' establishes that His knowledge is an essential attribute, not contingent on the existence of created beings, thereby preserving absolute monotheism without compromising divine omniscience.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 11. Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-`Attar (RA) said, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad, on the authority of al-Husayn ibn Sa`id, on the authority of alQasim ibn Muhammad, on the authority of `Abd al-Samad ibn Bashir, on the authority of Fudayl ibn Sukkarah

that I asked Abu Ja`far al-Baqir (AS): May I be taken as your ransom! I hope that you can tech me. Prior to creation, did Allah, may His Remembrance be Exalted, know that He was One? Your followers have a dispute regarding this issue. Some of them say: “The Blessed and Exalted surely knew that He was alone before He created anything from His Creation/” While others say: “Verily, the meaning of knowing is doing. Therefore, He knows today that there was no one other than Him before He created the thngs.” And they say: “If we prove that He has always known that ere was none but Him, then we have proved that there was other than Him in sempiternity [azaliyyah]. If you could be so kind, O my Master, to teach me whether the truth is other than this. Thus, he (AS) wrote: “Allah, the Exalted, has always been All-Knowing, Blessed and Exalted be His Remembrance.”
